1	/**
2	 * Host-level capacity accounting for freemc-host — the single shared Docker
3	 * box every free-tier Minecraft container runs on (see the module doc atop
4	 * lib/free-minecraft-control.ts for the product's overall architecture).
5	 *
6	 * freemc-host is small and FIXED: confirmed live (2026-08-25) at 7.8GB RAM
7	 * and only 3 vCPUs. recreateGameTypeContainer already assigns each container
8	 * --cpus (2 for a kind:"plugins" type, 1 for kind:"properties"/vanilla) and
9	 * --memory (>=2560m for plugins, else the configured free_minecraft_ram_mb).
10	 * Do the math: this host can run at most ONE plugin-kind server (2 of 3
11	 * vCPUs) plus one vanilla-kind server (1 vCPU) awake at once before CPU
12	 * oversubscription — RAM has more headroom, CPU is the binding constraint.
13	 *
14	 * This is deliberately NOT a queue system — just an honest "are we full"
15	 * check the paths we control (create / switch type / manual dashboard start)
16	 * can consult before starting one more container than the host can actually
17	 * run. The passive mc-router wake path (a third-party Go proxy that runs
18	 * `docker start` on its own, outside this app) is explicitly out of scope —
19	 * we don't control it and can't gate it from here.
20	 *
21	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from free-minecraft-control.ts,
22	 * lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts, and lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts, matching
23	 * the same plain-module convention as ssh-exec.ts and free-minecraft-control.ts.
24	 */
25	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
26	import { exec, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
27	
28	/** Free-tier container name prefix — see FreeMinecraftServer.containerName's
29	 *  schema comment (`mc-free-<userId>`) and lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts's
30	 *  `createFreeMinecraftServer`, the one place that derives it. Every capacity
31	 *  computation here filters to exactly this prefix so it only ever sums
32	 *  free-tier containers, never anything else that might run on this host. */
33	export const FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX = "mc-free-";
34	
35	export type RunningFreemcContainer = {
36	  containerName: string;
37	  cpus: number;
38	  ramMb: number;
39	  /** `docker inspect .State.StartedAt`, RFC3339 — empty string if unavailable. */
40	  startedAt: string;
41	};
42	
43	export type FreemcHostCapacity = {
44	  /** From a live `nproc` on the host — checked fresh every call rather than
45	   *  hardcoded, so a future host resize is picked up automatically. */
46	  totalCpus: number;
47	  /** From a live `free -m` on the host. */
48	  totalRamMb: number;
49	  /** Sum of --cpus across every RUNNING (not stopped/exited) free-mc container. */
50	  committedCpus: number;
51	  /** Sum of assigned --memory (MB) across every RUNNING free-mc container. */
52	  committedRamMb: number;
53	  runningContainers: RunningFreemcContainer[];
54	};
55	
56	/**
57	 * Safety margin reserved for the OS/Docker daemon itself, never handed out to
58	 * customer containers. Checked live against freemc-host's actual idle
59	 * baseline (2026-08-25, with every free-mc container stopped except the
60	 * always-on mc-router): `top`/`mpstat` showed 0.0-0.3% CPU busy (mc-router
61	 * itself: 0.02% CPU via `docker stats`) and `free -m` showed only ~592MB
62	 * "used" (out of 7941MB — the other ~2GB "buff/cache" is reclaimable, not a
63	 * real commitment) for the kernel, sshd, dockerd, containerd, and mc-router
64	 * combined. So idle overhead alone would justify a far smaller margin than
65	 * what's reserved here — this is a deliberately conservative buffer on top of
66	 * that idle baseline, not a measurement of steady-state need, sized for
67	 * bursty admin/maintenance load this idle snapshot doesn't capture: docker
68	 * image pulls/plugin downloads, log rotation, cron sweeps, and an admin SSH
69	 * session running docker/inspect commands like this very check. On a
70	 * 3-vCPU host, holding back 1 whole vCPU (33%) is a big fraction, but it's
71	 * simple, easy to reason about, and means the one "spare" core is never fully
72	 * shared away — better to run one fewer plugin-kind server than to risk
73	 * starving the daemon that manages all of them. Concretely, with this
74	 * margin: the host can run ONE plugin-kind server (2 vCPU) alone, or up to
75	 * TWO vanilla-kind servers (1 vCPU each) together, but NOT one plugin-kind
76	 * plus one vanilla-kind at once (2+1=3 exceeds the 2-vCPU margined budget) —
77	 * tighter than the zero-margin hardware ceiling this file's module doc
78	 * describes, by design.
79	 */
80	export const FREEMC_RESERVED_CPUS = 1;
81	export const FREEMC_RESERVED_RAM_MB = 1024;
82	
83	/**
84	 * Live capacity snapshot: host totals + what every running free-mc container
85	 * has actually been assigned, straight from `docker inspect` (the same
86	 * NanoCpus/.HostConfig.Memory fields recreateGameTypeContainer's --cpus/
87	 * --memory flags produce) — never trusted from the DB, since the DB doesn't
88	 * track per-container resource assignment at all.
89	 */
90	export async function getFreemcHostCapacity(conn: Client): Promise<FreemcHostCapacity> {
91	  const [nprocRes, freeRes, psRes] = await Promise.all([
92	    exec(conn, "nproc", 10_000),
93	    exec(conn, "free -m", 10_000),
94	    exec(
95	      conn,
96	      // ^/mc-free- anchors to the start of the container name so this can
97	      // never accidentally match some unrelated container that merely
98	      // contains the substring.
99	      `docker ps --filter ${shellQuote(`name=^/${FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX}`)} --format '{{.Names}}'`,
100	      10_000,
101	    ),
102	  ]);
103	
104	  const totalCpus = Number.parseInt(nprocRes.stdout.trim(), 10) || 1;
105	
106	  let totalRamMb = 0;
107	  const memLine = freeRes.stdout.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith("Mem:"));
108	  if (memLine) {
109	    const col = memLine.trim().split(/\s+/)[1];
110	    totalRamMb = Number.parseInt(col, 10) || 0;
111	  }
112	
113	  const names = psRes.stdout
114	    .split("\n")
115	    .map((s) => s.trim())
116	    .filter((s) => s.startsWith(FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX));
117	
118	  const runningContainers: RunningFreemcContainer[] = [];
119	  for (const name of names) {
120	    const inspect = await exec(
121	      conn,
122	      `docker inspect ${shellQuote(name)} --format '{{.HostConfig.NanoCpus}} {{.HostConfig.Memory}} {{.State.StartedAt}}'`,
123	      10_000,
124	    );
125	    if (inspect.code !== 0) continue; // container disappeared between `ps` and `inspect` — skip, not fatal
126	    const [nanoCpusRaw, memBytesRaw, startedAt] = inspect.stdout.trim().split(/\s+/);
127	    const nanoCpus = Number.parseInt(nanoCpusRaw, 10) || 0;
128	    const memBytes = Number.parseInt(memBytesRaw, 10) || 0;
129	    runningContainers.push({
130	      containerName: name,
131	      cpus: nanoCpus / 1e9, // NanoCpus is --cpus * 1e9
132	      ramMb: Math.round(memBytes / (1024 * 1024)),
133	      startedAt: startedAt ?? "",
134	    });
135	  }
136	
137	  const committedCpus = runningContainers.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.cpus, 0);
138	  const committedRamMb = runningContainers.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.ramMb, 0);
139	
140	  return { totalCpus, totalRamMb, committedCpus, committedRamMb, runningContainers };
141	}
142	
143	/**
144	 * Would starting one more container with the given cpus/ramMb push committed
145	 * usage past the safety-margined budget (total minus the reserved OS/Docker
146	 * slice)? Used by every path that's about to turn a container from
147	 * stopped/nonexistent into running — never by the mc-router passive-wake
148	 * path, which this app doesn't control (see this file's module doc).
149	 */
150	export function wouldExceedFreemcCapacity(
151	  cap: FreemcHostCapacity,
152	  addCpus: number,
153	  addRamMb: number,
154	): { exceeds: boolean; dimension?: "CPU" | "RAM" } {
155	  const cpuBudget = cap.totalCpus - FREEMC_RESERVED_CPUS;
156	  const ramBudget = cap.totalRamMb - FREEMC_RESERVED_RAM_MB;
157	  if (cap.committedCpus + addCpus > cpuBudget) return { exceeds: true, dimension: "CPU" };
158	  if (cap.committedRamMb + addRamMb > ramBudget) return { exceeds: true, dimension: "RAM" };
159	  return { exceeds: false };
160	}

content.content:
**Revises the Phase 1 write-up's gate above**: node-2 now meets the bar that section set ("only flip
`node-2.enabled` once Phase 3's node-agent + NAT sync is live and re-verified with an actual
external SSH connection succeeding") — that connection has now genuinely succeeded. Flipping
`enabled: true` is being left as a deliberate, separate decision rather than folded into this
verification pass, since it starts directing real customer signups to a second physical datacenter —
a product decision, not just a technical one.

### node-2 enabled + the free Minecraft host migrated to it (2026-09-05)

Same day as Phase 3 shipped, `node-2.enabled` was flipped to `true` and `freemc-host` — the real,
live, shared Docker host behind the free Minecraft tier (14 real customer worlds at the time) — was
moved from the primary to node-2. First real production use of everything Phases 1-3 built.

**How it worked out, since none of this needed new code**: `freemcHost()` (`lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`)
already selected `node.publicIp` (Phase 2), and the port-forwards for its SSH admin port and the
public Minecraft port (25565) already existed as ordinary `PortForward` rows — meaning moving the
VM's `nodeId` was the ONLY database change needed to make every dashboard control (power, console,
RCON, players) and the NAT layer follow it automatically. The actual VM move itself used the same
`vzdump`/`qmrestore` technique already established for cross-node template copying: live
snapshot-mode backup on the primary (zero downtime for that step, ~8.4GB compressed), transferred and
restored on node-2 under a fresh vmid, network config updated for node-2's own subnet
(`10.20.1.100/24`), and the stale `cicustom` reference (pointing at a per-VM snippet that only ever
existed on the primary) explicitly deleted — safe here specifically BECAUSE this is a restore of an
already-fully-configured disk, not a fresh template clone: nothing about this VM's working state
(Docker, mc-router, all 14 worlds' data) depends on cloud-init re-applying anything, unlike a brand
new provision.

**One piece IS genuinely external to this codebase**: the free tier's DNS. Free-tier subdomains all
share ONE wildcard `A` record (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) rather than the per-server A+SRV pairs
`lib/game-subdomain-dns.ts` manages for paid servers — mc-router resolves the right backend from the
Minecraft protocol's own hostname field (a per-container Docker label), not from DNS or from a
distinct port per world. That ONE wildcard record was updated by hand (Cloudflare API, platform
token) from the primary's IP to node-2's — there is no code path that manages it today, since it was
never expected to need to move before this.

**Cutover sequencing, in case node #3 or a future re-migration needs the same playbook**: stop the
old VM first (prevents any chance of both copies' mc-router simultaneously claiming the same
worlds), THEN move the DB row (this is what makes `syncPortForwards()` remove the old DNAT rule and
add the new one on its very next run — no manual iptables work either side), THEN flip DNS last (by
the time it propagates, the new path is already fully live). Verified after cutover with a real
hand-rolled Minecraft Server List Ping (protocol-level, not just a raw TCP check) against a real
customer subdomain, through mc-router, on node-2 — got back mc-router's own accurate "server is
asleep" status for that exact world, proving the full chain (DNS → node-2 NAT → guest → mc-router →
correct per-world routing) rather than just reachability. Only destroyed the old VM on the primary
after that.

**Timing note**: done with zero customers online (confirmed via `FreeMinecraftServer` — 0 of 14 worlds
running at the time), which is exactly why this was safe to do immediately rather than scheduling a
maintenance window — there's no way to get a lower-risk moment for a shared host like this than
"currently idle."

**Follow-up, same day, found live by the owner**: `freemcHost()` in `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` was
fixed in Phase 2 (selects `node.publicIp`), but it turns out **five other files each hand-roll their own
identical copy** of that helper — `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts`,
`lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts` — none of
which got the fix, because the earlier audit only searched for call sites of the customer-facing one, not
every place the same 5-line function was independently reproduced. Surfaced by the owner's screenshot of
`/admin/free-minecraft` showing "Could not reach the free Minecraft host." after the move (the admin panel
and roles/mods/inventory/worlds management were broken for every free account, even though the
customer-facing create/power/console paths worked fine). Fixed all five identically; verified live by
calling `connectionTarget()` directly against production and confirming it resolves to node-2
(`178.63.94.114:20002`), not the primary's fallback IP. **Standing lesson, not just for this host:**
whenever a shared connection-target helper changes shape, grep for every literal occurrence of its
defining condition (here, `hostname: "freemc-host"`) across the repo — a helper that isn't exported and
reimplemented per-file (a deliberate "file isolation" convention in this product's admin actions) means
one fix does not propagate, and nothing but a full grep catches the rest.

**A second, unrelated bug found the same night, also live**: a plain vanilla free server got OOM-killed
mid-session under completely ordinary gameplay (a player generating fresh terrain) — 870MB JVM heap
inside a 1024MB container (the non-plugins `jvmRatio` of 0.85 in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) left too
little headroom for the JVM's own non-heap overhead (metaspace, thread stacks, NIO direct buffers), and
real RSS hit 1041MB, over the cgroup limit — confirmed via `dmesg`'s `oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG`
entry naming the java process. This is the exact bug class the file's own inline history already documents
fixing for `kind:"plugins"` presets (see the comment above `jvmRatio`'s definition) — the vanilla ratio
had the same flaw, just a smaller, rarer margin. Fixed: 0.75 for non-plugins presets (768MB heap / 256MB
headroom instead of 870/154m). Left the global `free_minecraft_ram_mb` default (1024) untouched — that's
a capacity/cost decision, this was a correctness fix within the existing limit.

**A costly lesson learned applying that fix to already-running containers**: `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`'s
own module doc states plainly that freemc-host's 3 vCPUs (1 reserved) support **at most 2 concurrently
RUNNING vanilla-kind containers** — everything else is supposed to be asleep, woken on demand by
mc-router. `recreateGameTypeContainer` does `docker rm -f` on the old container **unconditionally, before**
its capacity check — so recreating an already-running container is capacity-neutral (its own usage frees
the instant before the new one is counted), but recreating a *sleeping* one is a net-new commitment. A
sweep to apply the new ratio to every vanilla container, done without first checking which ones were
actually running, woke several sleeping containers, exhausted the entire 2-vCPU budget within the first
two, and then cascaded into deleting (not stopping — `docker rm -f` had already run) the container of the
one customer who really was connected, when its own recreate attempt failed the capacity check with
nothing left to roll back to. World data was untouched (it lives on a bind mount at
`/opt/freemc/servers/<FreeMinecraftServer.id>`, independent of the container), and all affected servers
were restored within minutes by recreating one at a time and explicitly `docker stop`-ing anything that
wasn't running before touching the next one. **Standing rule for any future bulk maintenance across
free-mc containers: check `docker ps` first, process one container at a time, and put back to sleep
anything that wasn't already awake before you touched it — never assume a recreate is free just because
the old container is removed first.**


`npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Not deployed — commits land on `main` per this session's process
constraints; a separate promotion step applies the build.

---

## 2026-09-20 — mc-router wake-from-sleep race fixed: patched + rebuilt the binary (infra, not app code)

**The bug, confirmed live:** every free-tier Minecraft server's first connection attempt after
waking from sleep could get an immediate "Connection reset" (0 bytes either direction), forcing the
player to reconnect. Reproduced and root-caused on `freemc-host` (node-2, vmid 100,
`178.63.94.114:20002`) against `frostmc.play.nxeon.cloud` for real player `papiguapo`:
`docker logs mc-router` showed `"Woke up backend server"` immediately followed by `"Finished relay
frontend->backend" amount=0` and `"Finished relay backend->frontend" amount=0` — mc-router declared
the backend awake and relayed the player's real login packet before the Minecraft server was
actually able to answer it. A retry moments later succeeded normally, matching the intermittent,
race-condition shape of the bug.

**Root cause, found by reading `itzg/mc-router`'s actual source** (the container's own `--version`
reported `1.46.4`, commit `4a9ffa40cd6182d47e661001fae4ed278a0401e4`, matched exactly against
`github.com/itzg/mc-router` at that commit): `server/docker.go`'s `makeWakerFunc` — the function that
starts a sleeping container and decides when it's "ready" — only did a raw `net.DialTimeout` TCP
check in a poll loop. A bare TCP accept can happen slightly before the Minecraft server's own
protocol handler is wired up to process packets, so the very next thing mc-router does (dial again
and relay the player's already-buffered login bytes) can land in that gap and get reset. Checked for
a real fix first, per policy: no released version up to the latest at the time (`v1.47.1`,
2026-09-18) adds a protocol-level readiness gate — the CLI does have `-auto-scale-asleep-motd` /
`-auto-scale-loading-motd` (already configured on this host since 2026-08-24), but those only cover
STATUS-state server-list pings, never the LOGIN-state connection that actually triggers a wake, so
they couldn't have closed this gap. Docker labels `mc-router.auto-scale-wait-timeout` /
`-failed-motd` / `-restart-delay-motd` exist as constants in that version's source but are dead code
— declared, never read anywhere. The itzg/minecraft-server image already ships a real
protocol-level healthcheck (`mc-health`, visible via `docker inspect`'s `.State.Health`), but
mc-router's waker never consults container health either — it was strictly weaker than data already
available on the host.

**The fix:** forked `itzg/mc-router` at the exact running commit, added
`server/readiness_probe.go` (`probeMinecraftStatus`) — a minimal real Handshake + Status Request +
Status Response round-trip using the project's own `mcproto` package (no new dependencies) — and
changed `makeWakerFunc`'s poll loop in `server/docker.go` to only declare the backend "woken" once
that real protocol probe succeeds, not just the bare TCP dial. Every existing flag, timeout, and
behavior is unchanged for containers that are already fully up. Added
`server/readiness_probe_test.go` with three unit tests, including one that opens a listener which
accepts the TCP connection and then hard-resets it (`SetLinger(0)`) with no protocol response —
reproducing the exact live bug in isolation — and asserts the probe correctly reports "not ready"
rather than "success". `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...` all clean against the upstream test suite
too.

**How it was deployed (infra-only, no `/opt/nxeon` app code changed except this doc):** cross-compiled
the patched binary locally (`CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`), uploaded it to `freemc-host`,
and built a new image (`nxeon/mc-router:readiness-gated-v1`) by `docker create`-ing a throwaway
container from the exact running image digest
(`itzg/mc-router@sha256:92766cd72262e4e13569463708af2bb87457ee5b3ba914b72ccbc8b09f8eb384`), `docker
cp`-ing the patched binary over `/mc-router`, and `docker commit`-ing — this never touched the live
`mc-router` container while building. Verified the new image side-by-side with the live one first
(a second, unpublished-port `mc-router` instance on the same `freemc` Docker network, discovering the
same containers via the same labels) before touching production. Swapped only once live connections
on the public port were confirmed at zero (`ss -tn state established`): `docker stop` + `docker
rename mc-router mc-router-old-itzg-backup` (kept, stopped, as an instant rollback — not deleted),
then `docker run` the new image with byte-for-byte identical name/flags/network/port/mount/user/
restart-policy. Clean startup, all existing routes rediscovered correctly.

**Real end-to-end verification, not simulated:** wrote a standalone Python script
(`/root/mc_login_probe.py` on freemc-host) that speaks a real Minecraft LOGIN-state handshake
(Handshake → Login Start) over a raw socket — used it against a genuinely asleep, non-paying-customer
free server both before and after the swap. Confirmed the exact live bug signature was reproducible
against the pre-patch image's own waker logic in isolation, then confirmed the patched, now-live
`mc-router` woke `rocket.play.nxeon.cloud` from a real sleep and returned a real 70-byte protocol
response on the very first attempt (`docker logs`: `"Woke up backend server"` only logged once the
real probe succeeded, immediately followed by `"Finished relay backend->frontend" amount=70` — no
0-byte reset).

**Blast radius / safety notes for whoever touches this host next:** `freemc-host` is memory-tight
(1.8GB total RAM) — the documented "at most ~2 vanilla containers running at once" capacity ceiling
in `lib/freemc-capacity.ts` is real and was felt directly during this fix's own testing (SSH banner
exchange itself started timing out under load average ~11 with 2 free-tier JVMs briefly awake at
once). Avoid waking more than one or two extra containers at a time for any future diagnostics here.
There is no docker-compose file or systemd unit for `mc-router` on this host — it was originally
started with a bare `docker run --restart unless-stopped ...` and nothing in `/opt/nxeon` app code
recreates it, so `docker inspect mc-router` is the actual source of truth for its current
config/image/flags going forward. `mc-router-old-itzg-backup` (the pre-patch container, stopped) was
intentionally left in place as a same-command rollback; safe to `docker rm` once the patched image
has run cleanly for a while.

content.thinking:
This confirms it: at the OOM moment, the balloon had inflated to reserve 1636846 of 2097016 pages, meaning the guest's actual managed memory had shrunk to roughly 1.8GB despite an 8GB nominal allocation. A single plugins container pushing 1.5GB RSS against its 2.5GB limit, combined with mc-router, triggered the global OOM, even though 4GB of swap sat unused since it was marked unreclaimable.

The real issue is that the app's capacity check reads `free -m` total which drops under ballooning, so it would correctly refuse to start new plugins containers when memory is this constrained — but mc-router's wake path isn't gated by that check at all, since it just calls `docker start` unconditionally. That's the actual crash mechanism: mc-router waking containers with 1.5-2.5GB limits inside a VM that's been ballooned down to 1.8GB. Root cause traces back to Proxmox's autoballoon shrinking VM 100 toward its 2048MB minimum because node-2 is overcommitted (66GB allotted on a 64GB host), and the fix would be disabling the balloon device entirely or setting it to match full memory via `qm set 100 --balloon 0`, though that likely requires a VM reboot to fully take effect.

Now I'm looking at the severity of the memory pressure itself — cgroup stall totals showing over 1200 seconds of memory and I/O pressure, plus heavy guest-side swap usage, which explains the "very slow" symptom: once ballooned down, the JVM starts swapping heavily. I should pull the RRD data for VM 100 and node-2 to see the memory pressure history and balloon behavior over the past month, correlating it with the known crash timestamps — the Sep 6 exit-137 cluster matches the documented maintenance sweep, while the Sep 20 exit-255 looks like a genuine OOM kill.

That gives four confirmed global OOM kills this boot, all occurring while the VM was ballooned down to roughly 1.8GB. I also want to check earlier boots for similar cgroup OOM events, and there's a strange gap — boot -1 ended Sep 6 but the current boot didn't start until Sep 11, suggesting the VM might have been down for over four days despite Proxmox reporting 20 days of uptime. I should check node-2's task log for VM 100 to figure out what happened during that gap.

content.thinking:
Without Docker or Java available locally, I'll need to rely on known vanilla output formats for RCON parsing, flagging anything unverified. I'm recalling the vanilla `/tick query` response structure from Minecraft's source, which reports target tick rate, average tick time versus target, and percentile breakdowns (P50/P95/P99).

Paper's `tps` command returns color-coded output using § codes over RCON rather than ANSI, which I'll need to strip, while `mspt` reports avg/min/max tick times over different windows. Since Paper 1.20.3+ supports the vanilla tick command too, I'll prioritize `tps` with a fallback to `tick query`, keeping the parsing logic pure and testable. Now I'm sketching the file structure: a pure module for resource/JVM flag computation and capacity sizing, one for health parsing (docker stats, tick/tps data, crash classification, backoff logic), one for upsell trigger rules with cooldown logic, and a plain module for host-level concerns.

I'm planning the schema additions for FreeMinecraftServer along with new models for samples, events, upsell events, and start requests, then outlining the worker sweep logic that batches SSH commands for docker inspection, stats, RCON queries, player counts, log scanning for wake events, disk usage checks, trash purging, start-queue processing, and watchdog restarts — all feeding into the new sample/event tables and registered in the worker index. Finally, I'm noting the changes needed in the game type container recreation function to wire up JVM flags, memory settings, and engine selection.

I'm also flagging a concern: adding bounded log rotation flags and labeling containers, but worried about the default docker stop timeout potentially cutting off world saves during scale-down and causing corruption, so I need to check whether mc-router's stop call respects a configurable timeout.

Since no timeout is passed, it falls back to the container's own stop timeout, which is a cheap fix worth including since I've seen exit code 137s consistent with forced kills mixed with clean exits. I should also fix the plugin-data wipe issue where only jar files get deleted in world/mod/preset actions, switch world and server deletion to use trash instead of permanent removal, and look at how start capacity evaluation is used for creation and power actions to handle queuing.

Beyond that, I need to design the free Minecraft start request/cancel flow with a dashboard queue position indicator, build the upsell UI with a nudge component and comparison card backed by health/upsell actions and event logging, fix the broken dashboard deploy link, add a world export API route, and expand the admin page with health columns, an events feed, upsell funnel metrics, a sizing panel, and a queue view action.

Now I'm working through the rollout scripts, specifically figuring out whether setting the VM balloon min/max equal to disable ballooning takes effect live on a running VM or requires a pending hotplug change in Proxmox.

I'm also outlining remaining rollout steps like orphan cleanup with dry-run/apply and VM resizing requiring a reboot, plus listing the test files and documentation sections needed, and sketching out the settings keys for watchdog auto-restart, default engine, upsell, and queue behavior.

Since free_minecraft_queue_enabled is already registered, I should check how settings are wired through lib/actions-settings.ts and whether FreeMinecraftPanel.tsx needs updating — it's already mine to edit, so that's straightforward. Given the scope, I'll start with the schema and review the rest of the FreeMinecraftServer model along with the Setting helpers.

Tests are still waiting on the heavy lock, so I'll move on. I'm thinking about whether to add a doc note about the balloon problem in the capacity module—specifically whether `free -m`'s MemTotal reading reflects live ballooned memory, since virtio-balloon inflation actually does shrink reported MemTotal, which is useful context for the capacity check.

Now I'm sketching the worker health sweep function: it'll check the free_minecraft_enabled and health_enabled settings, find the freemc host, and open an SSH connection with timeouts to run the sweep logic.

I'm planning the sweep steps: inspect all mc-free-* containers in one batched docker exec, pull stats for running ones, then for each running container tick health checks via rcon (tps/tick query) and player counts (using mc-monitor or rcon list), capped at 10 containers per sweep. I'm also adding logic to parse mc-router logs since the last sweep for scale-up/wake events, mapping addresses to servers by subdomain and recording wake/failure events.

For exit detection, I'm comparing finishedAt against the stored lastExitSeenAt to classify crashes (OOM, KILLED, etc.), being careful that a forced `docker rm -f` leaves no inspect data and that a 137 exit code could just be a stop-timeout kill rather than a real crash. To avoid flooding events with old historical exits on first run, I'll timestamp each event using the actual finishedAt time and simply update lastExitSeenAt without emitting an event if the exit is older than 24 hours when first observed.

Now I'm working out the watchdog's restart logic: gathering recent crash times from OOM/CRASH events in the last 30 minutes, checking if players were online shortly before the crash, and deciding whether to issue a `docker start` with a WATCHDOG_RESTART event. Since restarts need a notBefore delay, I'm figuring out how to track "pending restart" state per container -- essentially checking at each sweep whether a stopped container has an unhandled crash event with no subsequent restart, then computing the restart decision from there.

I also need to handle the breaker logic, setting a crashBreakerUntil window and emitting a single BREAKER_OPEN event, while noting that the breaker can't actually prevent mc-router from waking idle containers -- that limitation just needs documenting. For running containers, I'm adding detection of "unhealthy" status via the itzg healthcheck, treating containers that have been up more than 5 minutes but report unhealthy as hung, and triggering a `docker restart` with backoff plus a WATCHDOG_RESTART event tagged "unhealthy" if auto-restart is enabled.

Next, the queue sweep should expire waiting requests older than 20 minutes, check if the oldest waiting request's container is already running (mark STARTED), otherwise evaluate available capacity and start one container per sweep with a QUEUE_STARTED event. Finally, I'm planning a periodic disk-usage scan every six hours to update size metadata per server directory, plus a trash-purge step that removes trash entries older than 7 days.

I also need new admin-facing settings keys for engine default, watchdog autorestart, upsell, and health check toggles — let me check the actions-settings structure to see where to slot these in.

/* ── one dial for icon size, site-wide ────────────────────────────────────
   Every mark in the system is drawn a fixed multiple of the size its call site
   asks for. Applying it HERE rather than editing hundreds of call sites keeps
   the relative sizing intact: an icon that was deliberately smaller than its
   neighbour stays proportionally smaller, it is just bigger in absolute terms.
   Change this one number to retune the whole set.

   Note for anyone adding a primitive: scale exactly ONCE per rendered mark.
   `Plate` draws an `Icon` inside itself, so it scales its own BOX and passes
   the raw size through — scaling in both places would compound to 2.25x. */
export const ICON_SCALE = 1.5;
export const iconPx = (n: number) => Math.round(n * ICON_SCALE);

/**
 * One interface mark.
 *
 * VECTOR FIRST, sprite as the fallback. `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` carries the set
 * redrawn as 24x24 paths; anything it defines renders as an inline SVG in
 * `currentColor`, and anything it doesn't — the sheet's brand row (linux,
 * docker, postgres…) and the five 3D product renders — still comes off
 * `public/nx/nxicons.webp` exactly as before.
 *
 * Why the switch is here rather than at 137 call sites: the sprite's marks are
 * pre-coloured, so one inside a tinted control renders in the SHEET's colour
 * instead of the control's (a teal shieldcheck on a violet "Admin" chip is the
 * bug that started this). Routing both through one component means every call
 * site gets `currentColor` without being edited, and a name with no vector yet
 * silently keeps working.
 *
 * `size` still means what it always did — ICON_SCALE is applied here for BOTH
 * paths, so a swap is 1:1 and `Plate` (which sizes its box with `iconPx`)
 * needs no change.
 */
export function Icon({
  name, size = 20, className = "", style, strokeWidth = 1.8, tone,
}: {
  name: string; size?: number; className?: string; style?: React.CSSProperties;

For existing servers to pick up new JVM flags, they need to be recreated since old containers keep stale config — so I'm planning a one-at-a-time recreate-while-asleep script using existing library functions: skip running containers, recreate each READY server, wait for it to boot, then immediately stop it again to return it to sleep, checking capacity between each one, defaulting to dry-run with an `--apply --limit N` option.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Free Minecraft stability rollout — STEP 1 (the root-cause fix).
#
# WHAT: stop Proxmox auto-ballooning from shrinking freemc-host (node-2, vmid
# 100). Its config has `memory: 8192, balloon: 2048`, so whenever node-2 sits
# above ~80% RAM, pvestatd inflates the balloon and the guest is left with
# ~1.8 GB usable. Every OOM kill in freemc-host's current boot (Sep 17 10:43,
# Sep 20 14:30 / 15:44 / 19:26) was a GLOBAL OOM inside such a window — the
# kernel's own OOM report shows 1,636,846 of 2,097,016 pages "reserved" by the
# balloon. Setting balloon == memory makes the floor equal the ceiling, so the
# guest always keeps its 8 GB. This is applied LIVE (balloon target changes are
# hot-applied by Proxmox) — no reboot, no container touched.
#
# SAFE / REVERSIBLE:
#   dry run (default) ... prints current config + node-2 commitments, changes nothing
#   --apply ............. qm set 100 --balloon 8192
#   --rollback .......... qm set 100 --balloon 2048 (the previous value)
#
# Run from the PRIMARY (it ssh's to node-2 as root, same as other node tooling).
# Owner-run only: this changes a live VM's memory policy on a shared node.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

NODE="${FREEMC_NODE:-root@178.63.94.114}"
VMID="${FREEMC_VMID:-100}"
MODE="${1:-dry-run}"

remote() { ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NODE" "$@"; }

echo "== freemc-host (vmid $VMID) memory config on $NODE"
remote "qm config $VMID | grep -E '^(name|memory|balloon|cores):'"
MEM=$(remote "qm config $VMID | awk '/^memory:/{print \$2}'")
CUR=$(remote "qm config $VMID | awk '/^balloon:/{print \$2}'")
CUR="${CUR:-unset}"

echo
echo "== node-2 RAM: physical vs guaranteed (non-ballooned memory + balloon floors)"
remote 'total=$(free -m | awk "/^Mem:/{print \$2}"); sum=0; for v in $(qm list | awk "/running/{print \$1}"); do m=$(qm config $v | awk "/^memory:/{print \$2}"); b=$(qm config $v | awk "/^balloon:/{print \$2}"); g=${b:-$m}; [ "$b" = "0" ] && g=$m; sum=$((sum+g)); done; echo "physical=${total}MB guaranteed_floors=${sum}MB"; free -m | head -2'

case "$MODE" in
  dry-run|--dry-run)
    echo
    echo "DRY RUN. Would run on $NODE:  qm set $VMID --balloon $MEM   (current balloon: $CUR)"
    echo "Raises the guaranteed total above by $(( MEM - ${CUR/unset/$MEM} )) MB. Check it stays well under physical."
    ;;
  --apply)
    if [ "$CUR" = "$MEM" ]; then echo "Already pinned (balloon == memory). Nothing to do."; exit 0; fi
    echo "Applying: qm set $VMID --balloon $MEM"
    remote "qm set $VMID --balloon $MEM"
    remote "qm config $VMID | grep -E '^(memory|balloon):'"
    echo "Done. Verify inside the guest in ~1 minute: MemTotal should read ~7.9 GB and stay there."
    ;;
  --rollback)
    echo "Rolling back: qm set $VMID --balloon 2048"
    remote "qm set $VMID --balloon 2048"
    remote "qm config $VMID | grep -E '^(memory|balloon):'"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 [--dry-run|--apply|--rollback]" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Free Minecraft stability rollout — STEP 2: orphaned data + containers.
#
# Found 2026-10-01: 85 data dirs under /opt/freemc/servers but only 42
# FreeMinecraftServer rows (43 orphan dirs, ~1.4 GB), plus 1 container with no
# row (mc-free-cmtmg7vgh0k4jhl771tavwm2y) and stopped test containers
# (mc-readinesstest2, mc-skyblocktiming). Orphans come from failed creates
# (fixed in code now: a failed create removes its own dir) and from accounts
# deleted while the host cleanup didn't run.
#
# SAFE / REVERSIBLE:
#   dry run (default) ... lists what it WOULD move/remove, changes nothing
#   --apply ............. MOVES orphan dirs to /opt/freemc/trash/<id>__orphan__<ts>
#                         (same filesystem: instant, restorable with a plain mv;
#                         the health sweep purges trash after 7 days) and removes
#                         orphan containers ONLY if they are stopped.
# Never touches a dir/container that has a DB row. Never touches mc-router.
#
# Run from the PRIMARY: reads ids from the prod DB (read-only query) and runs
# on freemc-host through node-2's qemu guest agent. Owner-run only.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

NODE="${FREEMC_NODE:-root@178.63.94.114}"
VMID="${FREEMC_VMID:-100}"
MODE="${1:-dry-run}"
ENV_FILE="${NXEON_ENV_FILE:-/opt/nxeon/.env}"

DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' "$ENV_FILE" | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"' | sed 's/?schema=public//')
IDS=$(psql "$DBURL" -At -c 'select id from "FreeMinecraftServer"' | tr '\n' ' ')
CONTAINERS=$(psql "$DBURL" -At -c 'select "containerName" from "FreeMinecraftServer"' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -n "$IDS" ] || { echo "Refusing: got zero server ids from the DB (wrong env file?)." >&2; exit 1; }
echo "DB rows: $(echo $IDS | wc -w)"

APPLY=0; [ "$MODE" = "--apply" ] && APPLY=1

read -r -d '' GUEST_SCRIPT <<EOS || true
set -u
keep=" $IDS "
keepc=" $CONTAINERS "
stamp=\$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
mkdir -p /opt/freemc/trash
n=0; mb=0
for d in /opt/freemc/servers/*; do
  id=\$(basename "\$d")
  case "\$keep" in *" \$id "*) continue;; esac
  s=\$(du -sm "\$d" | cut -f1); n=\$((n+1)); mb=\$((mb+s))
  if [ $APPLY = 1 ]; then mv "\$d" "/opt/freemc/trash/\${id}__orphan__\${stamp}" && touch "/opt/freemc/trash/\${id}__orphan__\${stamp}" && echo "moved \$id (\${s}MB)"; else echo "would move \$id (\${s}MB)"; fi
done
echo "orphan dirs: \$n (\${mb}MB)"
for c in \$(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E '^mc-(free-|readinesstest|skyblocktiming)'); do
  case "\$keepc" in *" \$c "*) continue;; esac
  st=\$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "\$c")
  if [ "\$st" = "true" ]; then echo "SKIP running orphan container \$c"; continue; fi
  if [ $APPLY = 1 ]; then docker rm "\$c" >/dev/null && echo "removed stopped container \$c"; else echo "would remove stopped container \$c"; fi
done
EOS

ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NODE" "qm guest exec $VMID --timeout 300 -- bash -c $(printf %q "$GUEST_SCRIPT")" \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get("out-data",""), end=""); e=d.get("err-data"); print(("STDERR: "+e) if e else "", end=""); print("[exit", d.get("exitcode"), "]")'

[ $APPLY = 1 ] || echo "DRY RUN — re-run with --apply to move the dirs to trash."

content.content:
# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|
| `2d8fedd` | Game servers renew at their game-plan price, not the base VPS plan | **Real.** `renewalQuote` delegates to `renewalCharge` and owns no arithmetic; a test asserts the file contains none. The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |
| `f28f15e` | Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt | **Real.** `packMetadata` throws before `checkout.sessions.create`; the sold price rides in metadata; the receipt attaches an invoice or points at billing history, never promises one it does not send |
| `3aa24d7` | Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF) | **Mixed by design.** The two auth lockouts and the NAT flush are genuinely fixed. Email verification is **complete and deliberately disarmed** — `email_verification_enforced` defaults to `false` because the platform's DKIM record is missing (gaps 1 and 9). Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |
| `7490131` | Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI | **Real.** Three launch blockers from `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, all reproduced in a browser and all byte-identical in production, plus the card-save UI that had been wrongly marked complete |
| `156b6ac` | Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run | **Real, and verified on the live queue** rather than asserted: jobs drain, the permanent path settles, notifications stopped climbing |
| `4ea9790` | Promo-basis proration, post-cutover TLS, 8 more migration defects | **Real.** `Server.termPromoPercent` makes the proration round trip net zero by construction; the TLS pass stopped being dead code; 4 rows backfilled from real billing records with 0 fallbacks |
| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

The through-line across all seven is the defect this codebase keeps producing in new places: **a second
definition of something that already had one.** A second renewal formula. A second promo basis. A
- **Fix**: new nullable `Server.guestSshPort` column (additive, `db push`'d — changes nothing for any
  existing server, since `null` falls back to `?? 22`, today's exact behavior). `connectionTarget()`'s
  dedicated-IP branch now reads `server.guestSshPort ?? 22` instead of a bare `22`. Selected into
  `lib/actions-files.ts`'s server query (the Files feature); `worker/firewall.ts` already `include`s
  the whole row so it picked it up for free. New unit tests in `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`
  pin both the override and the (unchanged) default. Admin server detail page now shows "Guest SSH
  port override" for any server with a dedicated IP, so this doesn't stay a hidden DB-only field.
- **The firewall side needed a second, separate finding**: even with the port fixed, `syncFirewall`
  would still fail — this guest's `iptables` (legacy) returns "Incompatible with this kernel" (likely
  1Panel's own nftables-only setup). Checked the LIVE guest directly: `iptables -L INPUT` showed only
  UFW's own chains (`ufw-before-input` etc.), policy DROP — confirming the platform's `NXEON_FW` chain
  has in fact never once been successfully applied to this guest, so there was nothing live to
  "detach". The customer's 6 stale `FirewallRule` DB rows are display-only leftovers; deleting them
  requires no guest-side sync (and syncing them now would risk appending a default-DROP that doesn't
  know about port 2222 — `FW_KEEP_OPEN_TCP_PORTS` only keeps 22 open — so deliberately did NOT trigger
  a sync). `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs are only ever created by `lib/actions-firewall.ts` on an explicit rule
  edit (confirmed — no periodic/cron trigger exists), so once those 6 rows are gone, nothing re-fires
  on its own.
- **Not yet done**: deleting the 6 stale `FirewallRule` rows was blocked by the auto-mode permission
  classifier ("Modify Shared Resources") on a direct DB write — needs the owner to run it or grant it.
  Worth a platform-wide follow-up too: any guest running an nftables-only setup (1Panel defaults to
  this) can never successfully use the panel firewall feature at all, independent of this port issue.

**Files:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`.

---

*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
(server migration).*
## Game servers

**What it does.** Sells per-game tiers (RAM/slots/price) that provision a VPS from a game OS template,
then exposes game-specific settings, SFTP access and auto-update.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Game servers                                        [ + New server ]  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  mc-survival    Minecraft (paper)   4 GB / 20 slots    RUNNING          │

p="docs/DOCUMENTATION.md"
s=open(p).read()
ref='''### Free Minecraft tier — stability, health sweep and the upgrade path (2026-10-01)

Reference for how the free tier is kept alive on its one shared host (`freemc-host`, node-2 vmid 100,
3 vCPU / 8 GB nominal, Docker + patched mc-router). Full investigation in Part VII
("Free Minecraft: crashes + slowness root-caused").

- **Per-container shape** (`lib/freemc-limits.ts`, unit-tested): vanilla 1536 MB / 1 vCPU, plugin types
  2560 MB / 2 vCPU; heap 70% of the limit, initial heap half of that. JVM flags are named explicitly
  (`FREEMC_JVM_XX_OPTS`: Aikar's G1 set minus `AlwaysPreTouch`, plus `ExitOnOutOfMemoryError`) — without
  them HotSpot picks SerialGC for a 1-CPU/<1792 MB container. `docker run` also gets `--restart=no`,
  `--stop-timeout=60` (mc-router's idle stop no longer SIGKILLs a world save after 10 s), log rotation
  (10 MB x 3) and a `nxeon.freemc.engine` label.
- **Engine**: `FreeMinecraftServer.engine` — NULL (every pre-existing row) keeps `TYPE=VANILLA`; new servers
  take `free_minecraft_engine_default` (default `PAPER`, pinned to `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION` + ViaVersion).
  A world is never migrated between engines behind the owner's back.
- **New-server defaults** seeded into `server.properties` before first boot (never env vars, so the player's
  Settings tab still owns them): view-distance 8, simulation-distance 6, max-players 10.
- **Capacity** (`evaluateStart`): count cap `free_minecraft_max_concurrent` + CPU/RAM budget after reserving
  1 vCPU + 1 GB. `recreateGameTypeContainer` now checks BEFORE `docker rm -f` (with its own running
  container subtracted) and returns `untouched` on refusal so callers skip a pointless rollback. A refused
  dashboard Start offers the **start queue** (`FreeMinecraftStartRequest`): the worker starts the oldest
  waiting server when a slot frees; requests expire after 20 min; the position shown is a real count.
- **Health sweep** (`worker/freemc-health.ts`, every 2 min, fire-and-forget, `free_minecraft_health_enabled`
  default on): `FreeMinecraftSample` (docker stats RAM/CPU, RCON `tps`/`tick query`, players) and
  `FreeMinecraftEvent` (CRASH/OOM/KILLED/HUNG/WAKE/WAKE_FAILED/BREAKER_OPEN/WATCHDOG_RESTART/QUEUE_STARTED/
  CAPACITY_REFUSED). Crash-loop breaker: 3 crashes in 30 min pauses starts for 30 min
  (`crashBreakerUntil`). Auto-restart of a server that crashed WITH players on is opt-in
  (`free_minecraft_watchdog_autorestart`, default off; backoff 0 then 5 min). Every 6 h: `du` per server
  (`diskMb`, soft quota vs `free_minecraft_disk_mb`) and purge of `/opt/freemc/trash` entries > 7 days.
  The breaker cannot stop mc-router's passive wake (mc-router is outside this app) — it blocks our starts.
- **Deletes go to trash**: deleting a server or a world `mv`s it to `/opt/freemc/trash/<id>[__world]__<ts>`
  (`moveToTrash`) — restorable with a plain `mv` for 7 days. Plugin changes delete only `plugins/*.jar`
  (`clearPluginJars`), never plugin data folders.
- **Observability**: player Overview tab shows a Performance card (only measured values); `/admin/free-minecraft`
  shows per-server health, the event feed, the upgrade-prompt funnel and a sizing table.
- **Upgrade prompt** (`lib/freemc-upsell.ts`, unit-tested; `free_minecraft_upsell_enabled`): shown only for a
  measured signal on that server — OOM (1+) or crashes (2+) in 7 d; memory >= 90% of limit in 3+ samples in
  24 h; TPS < 18 in 3+ samples with players on; player cap hit; disk >= 80% of quota; 2+ wakes >= 45 s; or on
  the Mods tab, the real Forge/Fabric limit. Evidence sentence quotes the numbers; comparison uses live
  `GamePlan` rows; CTA = `deployHref({service:"game", gameFamily:"minecraft", gamePlanId})`; "Not now" = 7-day
  cooldown. Funnel rows: `FreeMinecraftUpsellEvent` (SHOWN deduped per trigger/user/day, CLICKED,
  DISMISSED; nothing logged while an admin impersonates) — available to the insights funnel.
- **Keep your world**: `GET /api/free-minecraft/world-export?type=<gameType>` streams the caller's own world as
  .tar.gz (asleep servers only, rate-limited); the player uploads it to the paid server's file manager/SFTP.
  Automated free->paid transfer is NOT built: it needs a cross-node copy into a customer VM, a stopped paid
  server, folder renaming to its `level-name`, and Paper<->vanilla dimension-layout conversion — each a
  failure mode that should be a supervised Job, not a button. Documented as a follow-up.
- **Rollout scripts** (`scripts/freemc/rollout/`, owner-run, dry-run by default): `01-pin-guest-memory.sh`
  (balloon = memory on vmid 100 — the root-cause fix), `02-cleanup-orphans.sh` (43 orphan dirs / 1.4 GB +
  orphan containers -> trash), `03-recreate-asleep.ts` (give existing asleep containers the new flags, one
  at a time, straight back to sleep).

'''
anchor="## Build with AI — Claude Code on every VPS"
assert s.count(anchor)==1
s=s.replace(anchor, ref+anchor,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

  limit.** Kernel log: Sep 17 10:43, Sep 20 14:30 / 15:44 / 19:26, all `constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,
  global_oom`, the victim always a free-server `java` (1.5 GB RSS for plugin servers). The OOM report itself
  shows `2097016 pages RAM, 1636846 pages reserved` — the balloon had taken ~6.2 GB of the 8 GB guest,
  leaving ~1.8 GB. VM config: `memory: 8192, balloon: 2048`. node-2's RRD puts every one of those kills
  inside a window where the node sat above 80% RAM (pvestatd's auto-balloon threshold): Sep 17 04:30-20:30,
  Sep 20 09:30-20:30. Balloon stats: the guest has swapped in **86 GB** over a 20-day uptime (45.8M major
  faults) — that is the "very slow". The app's capacity check reads `free -m`, which shrinks with the
  balloon, so app-initiated starts were refused while mc-router (outside the app) kept waking servers into
  a guest with no memory. Earlier boot (Sep 5-6): cgroup OOMs, fixed then by the 1536/2560 MB floors.
- **SerialGC on every vanilla server**: `--cpus=1` + 1536 MB is below HotSpot's server-class threshold, and
  no collector was named (no `USE_AIKAR_FLAGS`, no `JVM_XX_OPTS`). Inferred from documented JVM ergonomics,
  not observed on a live JVM (none was awake; none was woken). Surviving logs: 5 "Can't keep up" lines of
  2.0-3.8 s, 4 of them 2-23 s after a player joined.
- **Plugin data wiped on every type switch and every mod-menu save**: `rm -rf /data/plugins/*` /
  `rm -rf <data>/plugins` deleted LuckPerms' H2 DB (Roles tab), IridiumSkyblock islands, Towny towns,
  Essentials homes and Prison mines along with the jars. The `docker exec` form also silently did nothing
  for an asleep container, leaving the old type's jars. Now `clearPluginJars` (jars + Paper's remap cache
  only, on the host path).
- **`docker rm -f` before the capacity check** in `recreateGameTypeContainer`: a refusal left the account
  with no container (the mechanism behind the 2026-09-05 sweep incident). Order reversed.
- **No stop timeout**: mc-router's idle stop uses the container default (10 s) before SIGKILL — short for a
  world save. Now 60 s.
- Housekeeping found: 43 orphan world dirs (1.4 GB) + 1 orphan and 2 test containers; container logs had no
  rotation; `free_minecraft_idle_minutes` is not read by anything (mc-router has `-auto-scale-down-after=15m`
  baked into its own `docker run`); the dashboard's "Compare paid plans" link pointed at
  `/dashboard/order/game?game=minecraft`, a route that does not exist; power-button errors were discarded
  (a capacity refusal looked like a dead button); server delete had no confirm and was `rm -rf`.
- **Load is light**: CPU averages < 0.5% across the 9 days of sysstat history, steal ~0, peak 2 servers awake
  at once (mc-router log since Sep 20), 52 measured wakes median ~28 s (23-33 s), plugin boots 15-46 s
  warm / 30-77 s cold. Capacity is not the problem today; memory being taken away is.

**Shipped (branch `fix/free-minecraft-stability-upsell`)** — see the reference section "Free Minecraft tier —
stability, health sweep and the upgrade path" under Game servers for the mechanics: `lib/freemc-limits.ts`,
`lib/freemc-health.ts`, `lib/freemc-upsell.ts` (all unit-tested), `worker/freemc-health.ts`,
`lib/actions-freemc-health.ts`, world export route, Performance + upgrade cards, admin health panels, start
queue, crash-loop breaker, trash instead of `rm -rf`, Paper default for NEW servers only. Schema (additive):
`FreeMinecraftServer.engine/crashBreakerUntil/lastExitSeenAt/diskMb/diskCheckedAt`, new
`FreeMinecraftSample`, `FreeMinecraftEvent`, `FreeMinecraftStartRequest`, `FreeMinecraftUpsellEvent`. New
settings: `free_minecraft_engine_default` (PAPER), `free_minecraft_health_enabled` (on),
`free_minecraft_watchdog_autorestart` (off), `free_minecraft_upsell_enabled` (on).

**Staged rollout (owner-run; nothing here has been applied)**
1. `scripts/freemc/rollout/01-pin-guest-memory.sh --apply` — `qm set 100 --balloon 8192`. Hot-applied, no
   reboot. Raises node-2's guaranteed floors from 49.2 GB to 55.3 GB of 64 GB. Rollback: `--rollback`.
   **This alone addresses every OOM kill observed this boot.**
2. Deploy the branch (db push is additive). Health sweep starts sampling; nothing restarts on its own
   (auto-restart is off). Watch `/admin/free-minecraft` for a day.
3. `scripts/freemc/rollout/02-cleanup-orphans.sh` (dry run), then `--apply` — moves orphans to the trash.
4. `npx tsx scripts/freemc/rollout/03-recreate-asleep.ts --apply --limit 3`, repeat — existing asleep
   containers adopt G1 flags / stop timeout / log rotation, one at a time, straight back to sleep.
5. Optional: turn on `free_minecraft_watchdog_autorestart` once the event feed looks sane.
6. Sizing, only if `CAPACITY_REFUSED` / queue events show real demand: **5 vCPU / 8 GB pinned** doubles
   concurrent capacity (2 -> 4 vanilla, 1 -> 2 plugin) with no extra node RAM (node-2 runs 27 vCPUs on 12
   threads at load ~0.8). 16 GB would need ~8 GB more than node-2 can guarantee today. vCPU change needs
   a VM reboot with every free server asleep.

**Not done / follow-ups**: mc-router's idle timeout still hardcoded on the host (recreating mc-router is an
infra change); automated free->paid world transfer (export + manual upload instead); TPS/`tick query`
parsing written from the documented reply format, not yet seen against a live reply; the crash breaker
cannot block mc-router's passive wake.

'''
anchor="*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md`"
assert s.count(anchor)==1
idx=s.index(anchor)
# put before the '---' line preceding the footer
prev=s.rfind("\n---\n",0,idx)
s=s[:prev]+"\n\n---\n\n"+entry.rstrip()+"\n"+s[prev:]
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
tail -c 600 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

**Agent F (freemc): partly done. The code is committed but has not been typechecked or tried in a browser.**

Branch `fix/free-minecraft-stability-upsell`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-freemc`. Commits: `b317f0c6f4` (pure logic + tests) and `7dc11fbc98` (everything else). Both are auto-pushed. Progress note: `/root/agent-notes/freemc.md`.

**Root cause, from read-only data on freemc-host (node-2, vmid 100)**
- **Ballooning takes the memory away.** All 4 OOM kills since the Sep 11 boot (Sep 17 10:43; Sep 20 14:30, 15:44, 19:26) were global OOMs, not container-limit kills. The kernel's own report shows 1,636,846 of 2,097,016 pages reserved by the balloon, leaving about 1.8 GB. The VM config has a 2 GB balloon floor.
- Each kill falls inside a window where node-2 was above 80% RAM, which is when Proxmox shrinks ballooned VMs. The guest has swapped in 86 GB over 20 days, which is the "very slow".
- **Vanilla servers likely run SerialGC.** They have 1 vCPU and no collector flag, so the JVM falls back to a single-threaded collector. This is inferred from JVM rules, not seen on a live server.
- **Plugin data was being wiped.** Every type switch and every mod-menu save ran `rm -rf plugins`. That deleted Roles, SkyBlock islands, Towny towns, homes and Prison mines.
- The container was removed *before* the capacity check, so a refusal left the server with no container at all.
- Smaller findings:
  - No stop timeout (a world save gets killed after 10 s).
  - 43 orphan world folders (1.4 GB).
  - The "Compare paid plans" link pointed at a page that doesn't exist.
  - Start/stop errors were thrown away, so a refusal looked like a dead button.
  - `free_minecraft_idle_minutes` isn't read by anything.
- **Load is light:** at most 2 servers awake at once, CPU averages under 0.5%, wake-ups about 28 s. Capacity today is 2 vanilla or 1 plugin server.

**What changed**
- **New logic files (pure, with tests):** `lib/freemc-limits.ts` (sizing, JVM flags, capacity), `lib/freemc-health.ts` (log parsers, crash backoff and crash-loop breaker), `lib/freemc-upsell.ts` (prompt rules).
- **Health check:** `worker/freemc-health.ts` runs every 2 minutes. It stores RAM/CPU/TPS/player samples, crash, out-of-memory and wake events, runs the crash-loop breaker and the start queue, measures world size, and purges the trash after 7 days. Auto-restart after a crash is off by default.
- **Container changes in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`:**
  - Explicit G1 flags, starting heap below the maximum.
  - 60 s stop timeout, log rotation, no Docker auto-restart.
  - Capacity checked before anything is removed.
  - Plugin changes delete jars only; deleted servers and worlds go to a 7-day trash.
  - New servers only get Paper plus lower view distance, simulation distance and player-cap defaults; existing worlds are untouched.
- **Upgrade prompt:**
  - It only appears when that server's own measurements justify it, and quotes the real numbers.
  - Comparison uses the live paid Minecraft plans from the database, with a link into the deploy wizard prefilled for Minecraft.
  - "Download this world" export route.
  - "Not now" hides it for 7 days; shown/clicked/dismissed events are logged.
  - A Performance card shows the player only measured values.
- **Admin:** health table, event feed, prompt funnel and sizing table on `/admin/free-minecraft`.
- **Rollout scripts** in `scripts/freemc/rollout/` (01–03), all dry-run by default.

**Schema (additive only):**
- New fields on `FreeMinecraftServer`: `engine`, `crashBreakerUntil`, `lastExitSeenAt`, `diskMb`, `diskCheckedAt`.
- New tables: `FreeMinecraftSample`, `FreeMinecraftEvent`, `FreeMinecraftStartRequest`, `FreeMinecraftUpsellEvent`.
- Four new settings.

**Files edited outside my area:** `worker/index.ts` (a 6-line hook to start the health check), `lib/actions-settings.ts` (4 settings keys).

**Verification**
- Unit tests: 24 of 25 passed on the first run. The failure (an apostrophe in the seeded `server.properties` text) is fixed but not re-run, and the sizing test was extended after that run.
- **`tsc` never ran:** the shared heavy-command lock timed out twice.
- **No Playwright or dev-server check**, because of disk pressure and lock contention.
- Both rollout shell scripts were dry-run read-only against the real host and report correctly.
- The text formats parsed from the server's TPS / tick-time replies have not been checked against a real server.
- Throwaway DB dropped, `.env` removed.

**Remaining:** run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` and fix errors; re-run the 3 test files; check the free dashboard and admin UI on mobile and in light mode; `git merge main`.

**Owner must run (nothing has been applied):**
1. `bash scripts/freemc/rollout/01-pin-guest-memory.sh --apply` — sets balloon to 8192 on vmid 100. This is the root-cause fix; it applies live with no reboot, and `--rollback` undoes it.
2. Deploy the branch.

**Agent F (freemc): partly done. The code is committed but has not been typechecked or tried in a browser.**

Branch `fix/free-minecraft-stability-upsell`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-freemc`. Commits: `b317f0c6f4` (pure logic + tests) and `7dc11fbc98` (everything else). Both are auto-pushed. Progress note: `/root/agent-notes/freemc.md`.

**Root cause, from read-only data on freemc-host (node-2, vmid 100)**
- **Ballooning takes the memory away.** All 4 OOM kills since the Sep 11 boot (Sep 17 10:43; Sep 20 14:30, 15:44, 19:26) were global OOMs, not container-limit kills. The kernel's own report shows 1,636,846 of 2,097,016 pages reserved by the balloon, leaving about 1.8 GB. The VM config has a 2 GB balloon floor.
- Each kill falls inside a window where node-2 was above 80% RAM, which is when Proxmox shrinks ballooned VMs. The guest has swapped in 86 GB over 20 days, which is the "very slow".
- **Vanilla servers likely run SerialGC.** They have 1 vCPU and no collector flag, so the JVM falls back to a single-threaded collector. This is inferred from JVM rules, not seen on a live server.
- **Plugin data was being wiped.** Every type switch and every mod-menu save ran `rm -rf plugins`. That deleted Roles, SkyBlock islands, Towny towns, homes and Prison mines.
- The container was removed *before* the capacity check, so a refusal left the server with no container at all.
- Smaller findings:
  - No stop timeout (a world save gets killed after 10 s).
  - 43 orphan world folders (1.4 GB).
  - The "Compare paid plans" link pointed at a page that doesn't exist.
  - Start/stop errors were thrown away, so a refusal looked like a dead button.
  - `free_minecraft_idle_minutes` isn't read by anything.
- **Load is light:** at most 2 servers awake at once, CPU averages under 0.5%, wake-ups about 28 s. Capacity today is 2 vanilla or 1 plugin server.

**What changed**
- **New logic files (pure, with tests):** `lib/freemc-limits.ts` (sizing, JVM flags, capacity), `lib/freemc-health.ts` (log parsers, crash backoff and crash-loop breaker), `lib/freemc-upsell.ts` (prompt rules).
- **Health check:** `worker/freemc-health.ts` runs every 2 minutes. It stores RAM/CPU/TPS/player samples, crash, out-of-memory and wake events, runs the crash-loop breaker and the start queue, measures world size, and purges the trash after 7 days. Auto-restart after a crash is off by default.
- **Container changes in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`:**
  - Explicit G1 flags, starting heap below the maximum.
  - 60 s stop timeout, log rotation, no Docker auto-restart.
  - Capacity checked before anything is removed.
  - Plugin changes delete jars only; deleted servers and worlds go to a 7-day trash.
  - New servers only get Paper plus lower view distance, simulation distance and player-cap defaults; existing worlds are untouched.
- **Upgrade prompt:**
  - It only appears when that server's own measurements justify it, and quotes the real numbers.
  - Comparison uses the live paid Minecraft plans from the database, with a link into the deploy wizard prefilled for Minecraft.
  - "Download this world" export route.
  - "Not now" hides it for 7 days; shown/clicked/dismissed events are logged.
  - A Performance card shows the player only measured values.
- **Admin:** health table, event feed, prompt funnel and sizing table on `/admin/free-minecraft`.
- **Rollout scripts** in `scripts/freemc/rollout/` (01–03), all dry-run by default.
